title: Programming for Engineers (MATLAB/Python)
description: Teaches MATLAB and Python for engineering computation—covering workflow, data structures, control flow, modular code, data handling, visualization, debugging, numerical methods, simulation, optimization, and an applied capstone.

topics.title: Engineering Programming Mindset, Tools, and Workflow
topics.description: Set up MATLAB and Python environments while learning how engineers translate physical problems into computational steps.

children.title: Problem formulation for computation
children.description: Students learn that engineering code starts with a physical question, assumptions, variables, and a plan before syntax enters the picture.

children.title: MATLAB and Python environments
children.description: This subtopic builds fluency in the tools students will use for assignments, labs, and future engineering work.

children.title: MATLAB desktop, editor, command window, workspace
Python interpreter, IDEs, virtual environments, Jupyter notebooks
packages and toolboxes: NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib, pandas
Engineering workflow habits
children.description: Good computational work needs organization, naming, documentation, and repeatable execution from the beginning.

topics.title: Variables, Data Types, Operators, and Expressions
topics.description: Use core language elements to represent quantities, formulas, units, and engineering calculations accurately.

children.title: Variables and assignment
children.description: Variables let students name engineering quantities and reuse them in calculations without hiding meaning.

children.title: Data types and precision
children.description: Students need to know how computers represent numbers and text so calculations do not quietly mislead them.

children.title: Expressions and operators
children.description: Expressions are the building blocks for formulas, model equations, and engineering calculations.

children.title: elementwise versus matrix operators in MATLAB

topics.title: Arrays, Vectors, Matrices, and Indexing
topics.description: Work with vectorized data structures that are central to MATLAB, NumPy, linear algebra, measurements, and simulations.

children.title: Array construction and indexing
children.description: Arrays are the native structure for data, signals, spatial grids, and engineering unknowns.

children.title: one-based MATLAB indexing versus zero-based Python indexing
Vector and matrix operations
children.description: This subtopic connects programming syntax to linear algebra and efficient engineering computation.

children.title: Data structures beyond arrays
children.description: Students learn when a table, list, dictionary, or structure is more appropriate than a plain numerical matrix.

children.title: MATLAB cell arrays, structures, and tables

topics.title: Conditionals, Boolean Logic, and Control Flow
topics.description: Build programs that make decisions based on thresholds, operating regimes, validation checks, and design constraints.

children.title: If/else decision structures
children.description: Conditionals allow code to react to engineering regimes, constraints, and validity checks.

children.title: Boolean logic and comparisons
children.description: Boolean expressions define the conditions under which decisions, filters, and safety checks occur.

children.title: tolerances instead of exact floating-point equality
Input validation and guard clauses
children.description: Students learn to protect calculations from invalid values before they produce misleading results.

children.title: domain checks for logarithms and square roots

topics.title: Loops, Iteration, and Vectorization
topics.description: Implement repeated calculations efficiently and decide when loops, vectorized operations, or built-in functions are the right tool.

children.title: For loops and while loops
children.description: Loops express repetition, convergence, time stepping, and processing of repeated measurements.

children.title: for loops over indices and values
Vectorization and built-in functions
children.description: Vectorization is central to MATLAB and scientific Python because it makes code shorter, clearer, and often faster.

children.title: array operations instead of scalar loops
built-in reductions such as sum, mean, max, and norm
Iteration patterns in engineering
children.description: Students connect loop mechanics to real tasks such as convergence, simulation, and parameter sweeps.

topics.title: Functions, Scripts, Modules, and Modular Programming
topics.description: Organize code into reusable components with clear inputs, outputs, documentation, and testable behavior.

children.title: Function design
children.description: Functions help students turn repeated calculations into named, testable, reusable tools.

children.title: multiple outputs in MATLAB and Python
Scripts, modules, and notebooks
children.description: Students learn the difference between quick exploratory code and reusable project code.

children.title: Documentation and interface clarity
children.description: Clear function interfaces make engineering code easier to review, reuse, and verify.

topics.title: Data Import, File Input/Output, and Engineering Data Cleaning
topics.description: Read, write, clean, and structure experimental, simulation, and tabular engineering data.

children.title: Reading and writing files
children.description: Engineers often begin with measured or simulated files, so students need reliable data access skills.

children.title: Data cleaning and transformation
children.description: Raw data usually needs units, missing values, filtering, and reshaping before analysis.

children.title: Engineering data provenance
children.description: Students learn to preserve where data came from and what processing steps changed it.

topics.title: Plotting, Visualization, and Communication of Results
topics.description: Create clear plots and visual summaries that support engineering interpretation and technical communication.

children.title: Core plot types
children.description: Plots make numerical results interpretable and help engineers notice patterns or errors.

children.title: line plots, scatter plots, bar charts
Plot formatting and readability
children.description: A correct plot still fails if labels, scales, or legends make it hard to read.

children.title: Communicating engineering results
children.description: Students learn to pair visual outputs with concise interpretation and defensible conclusions.

topics.title: Debugging, Error Handling, Testing, and Reproducibility
topics.description: Diagnose code behavior, handle failures, validate results, and make engineering computations repeatable.

children.title: Debugging strategies
children.description: Debugging turns confusion into evidence by inspecting state, isolating causes, and testing assumptions.

children.title: Error handling and robustness
children.description: Engineering code should fail clearly or recover predictably when inputs are imperfect.

children.title: Testing and reproducibility
children.description: Students learn to trust results by rerunning code and checking against known answers.

topics.title: Numerical Methods I: Roots, Linear Systems, Interpolation, and Curve Fitting
topics.description: Apply foundational numerical techniques to solve equations, fit models, and approximate engineering relationships.

children.title: Root finding
children.description: Root finding solves equations that cannot be rearranged cleanly, a common engineering modeling task.

children.title: Linear systems and least squares
children.description: Many engineering models reduce to systems of equations or best-fit parameter estimates.

children.title: Interpolation and curve fitting
children.description: Students approximate relationships between measured or simulated data points.

topics.title: Numerical Methods II: Integration, Differentiation, and Differential Equations
topics.description: Use computational tools to approximate rates, accumulated quantities, and dynamic systems described by ODEs.

children.title: Numerical differentiation and integration
children.description: Students approximate slopes and accumulated quantities from functions or data.

children.title: Initial-value ODE solving
children.description: ODE solvers model dynamic engineering systems such as motion, circuits, heat transfer, and reactors.

children.title: Stiffness and solver choices
children.description: Solver selection matters when dynamic systems have multiple time scales or stability restrictions.

topics.title: Simulation, Monte Carlo Methods, and Parameter Studies
topics.description: Explore uncertainty, sensitivity, and system behavior through repeated computational experiments.

children.title: Deterministic simulation
children.description: Simulation lets students explore system behavior without requiring a physical prototype for every scenario.

children.title: Parameter sweeps and sensitivity
children.description: Parameter studies show which assumptions or design variables most strongly affect outcomes.

children.title: Monte Carlo simulation
children.description: Monte Carlo methods help students study uncertainty, variability, and risk in engineering calculations.

topics.title: Optimization and Engineering Design Computation
topics.description: Use computational search and constrained optimization to support engineering design choices.

children.title: Optimization problem setup
children.description: Students learn to express design goals and limitations as computational objectives and constraints.

children.title: Numerical optimization tools
children.description: This subtopic introduces practical solvers without turning the course into a full optimization theory class.

children.title: Design tradeoff interpretation
children.description: Optimization output only becomes useful when students can interpret tradeoffs and check whether the answer is physically reasonable.

topics.title: Integrated Engineering Applications and Capstone Project
topics.description: Combine programming, data analysis, numerical methods, visualization, and documentation in an applied engineering project.

children.title: Applied engineering case studies
children.description: Case studies show how programming supports mechanics, circuits, fluids, thermodynamics, and data analysis.

children.title: fluid-flow pressure drop or pump curves
Capstone project workflow
children.description: A capstone helps students practice planning, implementation, validation, visualization, and reporting in one coherent task.

children.title: Professional code review and presentation
children.description: Students finish by communicating not only what their code produced, but why it is trustworthy.
